ai.description: This 5–8 cm frog has a globular body with a small head. It is yellowish-brown with irregular dark marbling and a shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercle on each hind foot for efficient burrowing.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Uperodon systoma* is best distinguished by its globular, bloated body and a distinct, pale, marbled pattern over a yellowish-brown, smooth-skinned back.
ai.habitat: *Uperodon systoma* inhabits semi-arid to moist deciduous forests, scrublands, and agricultural plains, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Marbled Globular Frog inflates its body into a round, balloon-like shape to appear larger and more difficult for predators to swallow.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon systoma* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of up to 2,000 eggs in temporary rain pools. It is an explosive breeder with aquatic larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Marbled Globular Frog is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to southern India at elevations up to 1,000m.
ai.callDescription: The Marbled Globular Frog emits a loud, high-pitched, metallic "peep" repeated in rapid, rhythmic pulses, typically heard near temporary rain pools during the monsoon.
